description: "Use emotional design to reduce frustration and support confidence through respectful messaging, transparent feedback, and user control, grounded in actual research."

# Emotional Design

## Procedure
1. Establish the authorized task, research evidence, tone conventions, and emotional-friction hypothesis. Store artifacts only in approved product-owned locations.
2. Map possible frustration, uncertainty, relief, and confidence to task moments. Label inferred feelings as hypotheses and request VOC validation rather than diagnosing users.
3. Design honest feedback, humane errors, reversible actions, and clear consequences. Delight must support the task, not exploit vulnerability or distract from risks.
4. Implement approved copy/behavior changes and verify accessibility, comprehension prerequisites, recovery, and retained functionality.
5. Route authorized research to VOC through Squad/Factory or the active permitted coordinator; do not assume this Fullstacker skill can directly invoke VOC. Ask ProductOwner to assess outcome impact. Report observed evidence separately from intended emotional effects.

## Completion Checks
The experience preserves autonomy and transparent choices. No guilt, deceptive scarcity, coercive loyalty, dark patterns, or unsupported emotional/retention claims.

## Source
Original procedure informed by item 14 of [UX Playbook's UX skills article](https://uxplaybook.org/articles/top-skills-every-ux-designer-needs), accessed October 11, 2026.
